messages:
Marcus Li (Customer Success): FYI OakTree reported: their audit-export appears to be missing ~12 hours of entries tied to KMS key access. They see `403: key not found` in their download job and some api failures. Asking for scope and what to tell them about timeline.
Priya Patel (Support): Thanks Marcus. I triaged initial ticket — they attached the export job log and a couple of example request IDs. No PII flagged so far, but they are asking for an evidence timeline for legal. Escalating to eng+security. @Elliot @Danielle can you confirm next steps?
Elliot Chen (Eng-SRE): Looking. Can you paste a minimal log snippet and one request_id? also which env (prod/eu)?
Marcus Li (Customer Success): Sent via DM: env=prod-us, request_ids: r_2026-03-15_09a1, r_2026-03-15_11b4. Log excerpt:```2026-03-15T09:02:13Z export-job[424]: download failed: status=403 err="kms: decrypt failed: key not found"```
Priya Patel (Support): Repro steps from customer: 1) trigger audit export via console, 2) wait for job to move to COMPLETED, 3) download archive, 4) see 403 on some parts. They say re-trying after a few minutes sometimes succeeds for the same archive chunk.
Elliot Chen (Eng-SRE): Ok that pattern smells like KMS key lookup/replica inconsistency + transient auth. I'll check key metadata and recent rotations. Quick command to list key versions and CMK aliases I ran:```gcloud kms keys versions list --key my-cmk --location global```I'll also grep our key-lookup logs for the two request ids.
Danielle Rivera (Security): Important: before any key ops, we need to capture evidence (key metadata, key rotation events, access logs) for the customer. If a key rotation or accidental deletion happened we must document timeline and users with even-read access. Also: confirm whether this export contained any customer-supplied secrets or keys.
Elliot Chen (Eng-SRE): I pulled key metadata: no intentional rotation in last 30 days. There is a partial replication lag on one KMS region between 2026-03-15 08:50Z and 09:30Z — seeing KeyLookup errors correlated with their request timestamps. I attached snippet of internal lookup trace:```[2026-03-15T09:02:10Z] key_lookup id=k-123 region=us-west status=NOT_FOUND -> retry -> success at 09:02:12Z```That would explain intermittent 403s when the download reads different chunks hitting different replicas.
Marcus Li (Customer Success): If that's the cause, customer will want: 1) confirmation this was replication lag, 2) whether any keys were deleted/rotated, 3) timeline and when full integrity restored, 4) mitigation and prevention steps.
Danielle Rivera (Security): Confirming: no deletions or rotations recorded. Replication lag is still root cause candidate. For customer comms, we need to include: what was affected (audit export downloads for specific time window), whether any data was exposed (no evidence), and the remediation steps. Legal prefers a conservative timeline: window start = first observed NOT_FOUND (2026-03-15T08:50Z) to resolution (2026-03-15T09:30Z).
Priya Patel (Support): Can eng produce the evidence pack (key metadata, KMS audit entries, internal replica health metrics) and a succinct timeline we can send to customer? Also need confirmation whether to notify all customers or only OakTree.
Elliot Chen (Eng-SRE): I'll assemble evidence: key metadata export, replication metrics, and logs for the request ids. ETA 2 hours.
Danielle Rivera (Security): Security will validate evidence and draft the customer statement. Recommended language: "We observed transient KMS replication inconsistencies affecting audit export downloads for a limited window; there is no indication of unauthorized access or key deletion." We should offer OakTree an export retry and read-only re-generated archive.
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1479 (severity: low-medium) — assigned to eng-sre, security, support.
Marcus Li (Customer Success): Thanks. Priya, please coordinate a tentative customer update after we have evidence (Elliot + Danielle). Also add timeline for when we will notify if we discover any additional issues.
Priya Patel (Support): Will do. Proposed external timeline draft: initial acknowledgement within 1 hour (sent), evidence pack + recommended remediation within 4 hours, final closure within 48 hours unless new findings. Keeping customer notified.
Elliot Chen (Eng-SRE): Filed logs + metrics to the incident bucket: gs://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-1479/evidence.tar.gz. I also queued a short fix: increase KMS replica sync retries for export readers to reduce 403s. Patch will be staged and rolled in canary today.
Danielle Rivera (Security): Noted. Security review scheduled in 1 hour. If evidence changes (e.g., deletion), escalate to legal and update timeline.
Marcus Li (Customer Success): Good. I'll tell OakTree we'll send a detailed update after evidence validation, and offer to re-run the export now that the replica health shows steady-state.
Priya Patel (Support): Closing loop here: OakTree acknowledged and asked to be notified if scope widens. I'll post the evidence pack link in the ticket when it's ready. :thumbsup:
Elliot Chen (Eng-SRE): Follow-up: we confirmed no data loss, replication lag ~40m, mitigated by retry changes. Will monitor for 24h.
Danielle Rivera (Security): Final note: add the incident ID to the export logs and attach the audit of key admin actions. That ensures downstream compliance traces are complete.
Marcus Li (Customer Success): Thanks everyone — keeping this thread as the single source for comms.
